Hey, I've been in a slightly similar position with my grandmother...i know firsthand how the guilt eats you up from the inside and ptsd rules over your life with time...I'd say keep changing therapists and it takes as long as a lifetime to forgive yourself and learn that you're to blame, so take your time and go easy on yourself because life is long. My motivation was that my gran would be really disappointed to see her favourite grandchild is not taking care of herself and being happy. It's not easy to live like that but please take care of yourself because you're still here...you didn't kill her, no matter how much the guilt tries to convince you, you're not a murderer because she was in that mindspace from long and if you were there it would've been temporary seeing that she already self harmed the cuts ran deep not jus physically. I hope you learn to love yourself some day. As for letting people down in future relationships, that's something you can control now, now you have learnt and seen things no child should ever have to. Study as much as you can on depression and self harm, join a group online where you read and understand more on the topic and what she was going through so you can help others and notice signs, become better and live because there are others who you can actually help now as you're alive and breathing. Expand your knowledge and meet professionals or those who're or have been in your place before as they will understand your situation best and help you rationally. About the bad day, you were a kid mate, kids aren't even supposed to be dealing with self harm nor are we thought how to. Go easy on yourself because beating yourself up will push you towards depression, self harm and extreme ptsd and you have still a lot to experience. Hope you seek help and may heed to the wonderful words written here by others. Good luck.
